nodes.name: the strict partial order: conditions (C1)-(C3)
nodes.statement: \NI (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have $U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some $1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$; \NI (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where $\cle'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(\tilde{\clo}_d)'$; \NI (C3) $U\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{\clo}_d)''U^* \subset \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{\clo}_d)''E'_2$.

nodes.name: non-reflexivity and transitivity of $\prec$
nodes.statement: That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega) \prec (\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. By our starting assumption that $\clm' \neq \tilde{\clm}$ we check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in \clp$ there exists an element $\pi' \in \clp$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus $\clp_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$.

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality gives the contradiction
nodes.statement: However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset $\clp_0$ of $\clp$. We claim that $\pi_{max}=\oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in $\clp_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in \clp$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_1,\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in \clp_0$ there exists an element $(H_2,\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in \clp_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi_u$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_1 \raro n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in \clp_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph_0$. Thus by maximal property of $\clp_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{\clm}$ is a proper subset of $\clm'$. This completes the proof for (i) of (e) $\clm'=\tilde{\clm}$ when $P=Q$.
nodes.statement_short: A maximal chain has $\pi_{max}=\oplus\pi$ as an upper bound inside it, forcing $\pi_{max}\prec\pi_{max}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: proof of (f)
nodes.statement: In the proof of $\clm'=\tilde{\clm}$ in (e), we have used equality $P=Q$ just to ensure that $\Omega$ is also a cyclic for $\tilde{\clm}$ and $P=Q$ is used to prove $\pi(\clo_d)' = \pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''$. So (f) follows by the proof of (e).
nodes.statement_short: Only cyclicity of $\Omega$ for $\tilde\clm$ was used, so $P=[\tilde\clm\Omega]$ suffices.

nodes.name: proof of (g): the intersection identity $\bigcap_n \tilde\Lambda^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)')=\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\cap\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$
nodes.statement: A proof for (g) is given in [Mo3] with $\clm_0$. Here we will also give an alternative proof relating the criteria obtained in Proposition 3.4. To that end we claim that $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)')=\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)' \bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'.$$ That $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \{ \tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J: |I|=|J| < \infty \}'$ follows by Cuntz relation and thus $\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)') \subseteq \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For the reverse inclusion let $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'$. For $n \ge 1$, we choose $|I|=n$ and set $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I$. We check that it is independent of the index that we have chosen as $Y_n=\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J\tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_I\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_JX \tilde{S}_J=\tilde{S}^*_JX\tilde{S}_J$ where in second equality we have used $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ and also $\Lambda^n(Y_n)=\sum_{|J|=n } \tilde{S}_J\tilde{S}^*_IX\tilde{S}_I\tilde{S}^*_J=X$. This proves the equality in the claim. Going along the same line we also get $$\bigcap_{n \ge 1}\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\clo_d)') = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\bigcap \pi(\clo_d)'= \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \clo_d)'.$$
nodes.statement_short: Cuntz relations give one inclusion; setting $Y_n=\tilde S^*_IX\tilde S_I$ gives the reverse.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: purity as an asymptotic condition, via [Ar2] and [Mo3]
nodes.statement: By Proposition 3.4 $\omega$ is pure if and only if the set above is trivial. Thus once more by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] and Theorem 2.4 in [Mo2], purity is equivalent to asymptotic relation $||\psi \tilde{\tau}^n -\phi|| \raro 0$ as $n \raro \infty$ for any normal state $\psi$ on $\clm'$ ( Here we recall by Proposition 2.4 $P\pi(\clo_d)'P=\clm'$ as $P$ is also the support projection in $\pi(\clo_d)''\clf$ and support projection of $\phi_{\Omega}$ in $\pi(\clo_d)'$ is $\clf=[\pi(\clo_d)''\Omega]$, where commutant is taken in $\clb(\clk)$ ). By a duality argument Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3] we conclude that $\omega$ is pure if and only if there exists a sequence of elements $x_n \in \clm$ so that for each $m \ge 0$, $x_{m+n}\tau_n(x) \raro \phi(x)1$ as $n \raro \infty$ for all $x \in \clm \subseteq \clb(\clk)$. This completes the proof of (d) with $\clm$. For the proof with $\clm_0$ we need to show if part as only if part follows $\clm_0$ being a subset of $\clm$ and $\tau$ takes elements of $\clm_0$ to itself. For if part we refer to Theorem 3.2 in [Mo3].
nodes.statement_short: Triviality of that intersection is equivalent to $\|\psi\tilde\tau^n-\phi\|\to 0$, which a duality argument converts into the stated condition on $x_n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement:
First we will prove that $\omega$ is pure if $P$ is also the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''	ilde{\clf}$, where $	ilde{\clf}=[\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''\Omega]$. The support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''	ilde{\clf}$ is $	ilde{\cle}	ilde{\clf}$ and thus we also have $P = 	ilde{\cle}	ilde{\clf}$ by our hypothesis. Since $\Lambda^n(P)=\Lambda^n(\cle)\clf \uparrow \clf$ and now $\Lambda^n(P)=	ilde{\cle}\Lambda^n(	ilde{\clf}) \uparrow 	ilde{\cle}$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, we also have $\clf = 	ilde{\cle}$. Similarly we also have for each $n$, $\cle	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf)=	ilde{\Lambda}^n(	ilde{\cle})	ilde{\clf}$ and thus taking limit we also get $\cle=	ilde{\clf}$. \vsp So we have $P=\cle \clf=\cle 	ilde{\cle}=Q$. $	ilde{\clm}=P\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''P$ is cyclic in $\clk$ i.e. $[	ilde{\clm}\Omega]=[P\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''P\Omega]= P	ilde{\clf}=P\cle=P$ as $	ilde{\clf}=\cle$. \vsp However $ igcap_{n aro \infty} 	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)) = \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''  igcap \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ ( for a proof which is a simple application of Cuntz relation, we refer to section 5 of [Mo2]). Further $\psi$ being a factor state in $K_{\omega'}$, by Proposition 3.2 $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is a factor. In particular we have $ igcap_{n aro \infty} 	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d))	ilde{\clf} = \IC 	ilde{\clf}$. Thus by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] we conclude that $||\Psi \circ 	ilde{	au}_n -\phi|| aro 0$ as $n aro \infty$ for all normal state $\Psi$ on $	ilde{\clm}_0$ where $	ilde{\clm}_0=P \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''P$ as $	ilde{\clf}=\cle$ and support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $	ilde{\cle}$ and $P=\cle	ilde{\cle}\cle$. \vsp Note that $	ilde{\clm}_0 \subseteq \clm_0'$ where $\clm_0=P\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''P$. Further by Proposition 2.5 $\clm_0 = \{x \in \clm: eta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}\;\;\;$ and $	ilde{\clm}_0=\{x \in 	ilde{\clm}:  eta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}$. Once we set $P_0=[\clm_0\Omega]$ then we also have $P_0=[	ilde{\clm}_0\Omega]$ as $[	ilde{\clm}\Omega]=P=[\clm\Omega]$ by expending $u_z=\sum_{k \in \hat{H}} z^kP_k$ where $z aro u_z= PU_zP$ is a unitary representation of group $H$. \vsp For $x \in 	ilde{\clm}, y \in 	ilde{\clm}'$ we have $$\phi(	ilde{	au}(x)y)=\sum_k <	ilde{v}^*_k\Omega,x	ilde{v}^*_ky\Omega> = \sum_k <v^*_k\Omega,x y 	ilde{v}^*_k\Omega>$$ (as $v_k^*\Omega=	ilde{v}^*_k\Omega$ ) $$=\sum_k <\Omega, x v_kyv_k^* \Omega>=\phi(x 	au(y))$$ The dual group of $(	ilde{\clm},	ilde{	au},\phi)$ is given on the commutant by $(	ilde{\clm}',	au,\phi)$ where $	au(x)=\sum_k v_k x v_k^*$ for $x \in 	ilde{\clm}'$. where commutant is taken in $\clb(\clk)$. Now moving to $\{ eta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in the duality relation above, we verify that adjoint Markov map of $(	ilde{\clm}_0,	ilde{	au},\phi)$ is given by $(	ilde{\clm}'_0,	au,\phi)$ where $	ilde{\clm}'_0$, the commutant of $	ilde{\clm}_0$ is taken in $\clb(\clk_0)$ and $\clk_0$ is the Hilbert subspace $P_0$ with $\Omega$ as cyclic and separating vector for $	ilde{\clm}_0$ in $\clk_0$. Thus by Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3], there exists a sequence of elements $y_n \in 	ilde{\clm}'_0$ such that for each $m \ge 1$, $y_{m+n}	au_n(y) aro \phi(y)1$ as $n aro \infty$ for all $y \in 	ilde{\clm}'_0 \subseteq \clb(\clk_0)$. Thus $\omega$ is pure by Proposition 3.5 (e) once we recall $\clm'=	ilde{\clm}$ as $P=Q$ ( and so $\clm'_0 = 	ilde{\clm}_0$ ) by Proposition 3.5 (d). This completes the proof of purity property of $\omega$. \vsp In the following we now prove the hardest part of the theorem namely $	ilde{\clf}=\cle$ and $\clf=	ilde{\cle}$ if $\omega$ is pure. Proof uses extensively the general theory of quasi-equivalent representation of a $C^*$ algebra and we refer [BR1, Chapter 2.4.4] as a general reference. \vsp We set unitary operator $V=\sum_k S_k	ilde{S}^*_k$. That $V$ is a unitary operator follows by Cuntz's relations and commuting property of $(S_i)$ and $(	ilde{S}_i)$. Further a simple computation shows that $V\pi(x)V^*=\pi(	heta(x))$ for all $x \in \clb = \clb_L \otimes \clb_R$, identified with $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ and $	heta$ is the right shift. We also have  e 	heta(\cle)=V \cle V^*= \sum_{k,k'}S_k	ilde{S}^*_k \cle S^*_{k'}	ilde{S}_{k'}=\Lambda(\cle) \ge \cle \ee Similarly we also have  e 	heta(	ilde{\clf}) \ge 	ilde{\clf} \ee So in particular we have $V(I-\cle)V^* \le I-\cle$, i.e. $(I-\cle)V^*\cle=0$. Also for any $X \in \pi(\clo_d)'$ we have $V^*	ilde{\clf}X\Omega = 	ilde{\clf} \sum_k 	ilde{S}_k X 	ilde{S}_k^*\Omega$ as $S_k^*\Omega =	ilde{S}_k^*\Omega$. Thus $(I-	ilde{\clf})V^*	ilde{\clf}=0$ i.e. $V	ilde{\clf}V^*=\Lambda(	ilde{\clf}) \ge 	ilde{\clf}$. Similarly we also have  e 	heta^{-1}(	ilde{\cle})=V^*	ilde{\cle}V \ge 	ilde{\cle}\;\mbox{and}\; V^* \clf V \ge \clf \ee We also set two family of increasing projections for all natural numbers $n \in \IZ$ as follows  e \cle_n=V^n \cle (V^n)^*,\;\;	ilde{\clf}_n=V^n	ilde{\clf}(V^n)^* \ee \vsp Since $ eta_z(V)=V$ for all $z \in H$, $V \in \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by Proposition 3.4 as $\omega$ is pure. $\omega$ being also a factor state, we have $<f,V^ng> aro <f,\Omega><\Omega,g>$ as $n aro + \mbox{or} - \infty$ for any $f,g \in \pi(\clb_{loc})\Omega$ by Power's criteria [Pow] given in (1). Since such vectors are dense in the Hilbert space topology and the family $\{V^n:n \ge 1\}$ is uniformly bounded, we get $V^n aro |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology as $n aro + \mbox{or} - \infty$. \vsp For the time being we assume that $H$ is trivial. Otherwise the argument that follows here we can use for the representation $\pi_0$ of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ i.e. $\pi$ restricted to $[\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. \vsp We have following distinct cases: \vsp \NI { f Case 1.} $\cle 
eq I \;( 	ilde{\cle} 
eq I)$. Let $\cle_n aro \cle_{-\infty}$ as $n aro -\infty$ and thus $V\cle_{-\infty}V^*=\cle_{-\infty}$. We claim that either $\cle_{-\infty} = |\Omega><\Omega|$ or $\cle_{-\infty}$ is a proper infinite dimensional projection i.e. if $\cle_{- \infty}$ is a finite projection then $\cle_{- \infty}=|\Omega><\Omega|$. Suppose not then the finite subspace is shift invariant. In particular there exists a unit vector $f$ orthogonal to $\Omega$ such that $Vf=zf$ for some $z \in S^1$ and this contradicts weak mixing property i.e. $V^n aro |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology proved above as point spectrum of $V$ has only $1$ with spectral multiplicity $1$. \vsp If $\cle_{-\infty}$ is infinite dimensional we can get a unitary operator $U_0$ from $F_0=	ilde{\clh} \otimes_{\clk} \clh$ onto $\cle_{- \infty}$ and via the unitary map we can get a sequence of increasing projections $U_0\cle_nU^*_0$ in $\cle_{- \infty}$ and note that $U_0\cle_nU_0^*=V^nU_0 \cle U_0^*(V^n)^*$. Note that if $\cle_{- \infty}$ is infinite dimension the process will not stop in finite step. Thus we have $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{\cle}} F(k)$ where the index set is either singleton or infinity and each $F(k)$ will give a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$, where $F(1) =F_0-\cle_{-\infty}$. Further $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ being a simple $C^*$-algebra, each such imprimitivity system is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ [Mo3,section 4]: We fix a nonzero $f \in \cle-	heta^{-1}(\cle) 
eq 0$ otherwise $\cle=I$ as $	heta^n(\cle) \uparrow I$ as $n aro \infty$. $\pi_f:x aro 	heta^{-1}(x)f$ gives a representation of $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d=\clb_L$ and we check that $[\pi_f(	heta^{-1}(\clb_L)''f] \le \cle-	heta^{-1}(\cle)$ as $f \perp [	heta^{-1}(\pi(\clb_R)')\Omega] \ge [	heta^{-1}(\pi(\clb_L))\Omega]$. Thus simplicity ensures that $\cle - 	heta^{-1}(\cle)$ is a projection of dimension $\aleph_0$. Further $n_\cle$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$ since $F_0$ is separable. \vsp Since $	ilde{\clf}$ is also a proper projection, same argument is valid for $	ilde{\clf}$ with $	ilde{\clf}_{-\infty}= \mbox{lim}_{n aro -\infty} 	heta^n(	ilde{\clf})$ i.e. we can write $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{	ilde{\clf}}} 	ilde{H}(k)$, where each $	ilde{H}(k)$ give rises to a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$ where each system of imprimitivity is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ where $	ilde{F}(1) = F_0-	ilde{\clf}_{-\infty}$ and $n_{	ilde{\clf}}$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$. \vsp In the following we use temporary notation $H$ for Hilbert subspace $F_0$. For a cardinal number $n$, we amplify a representation $\pi:\clb aro \clb(H)$ of the $C^*$ algebra $\clb$ to $n$ fold direct sum $n\pi=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } \pi_k $ acting on $nH=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } H_k$ defining by $$n\pi(x) (\oplus \zeta_k) = \oplus (\pi(x)\zeta_k)$$ where $\pi_k = \pi$ is the representation of $\clb=\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes 	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ on $H_k=H$ where $H =[\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. We also extend $ ar{	ilde{F}} = \oplus 	ilde{F}_{\alpha}$, $ ar{E} = \oplus E_{\alpha}$ and $ ar{V}=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n} V_k$ respectively. We also set notation $\Omega_k=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}\delta^k_j\Omega$. \vsp Thus by Mackey's theorem, there exists a cardinal number $n \in \aleph_0$ and a unitary operator $U: nH aro nH$ so that $ ar{V}=U ar{V}U^*$ and $ ar{\cle}=U ar{	ilde{\clf}}U^*$. We set a representation $\pi^U:\clb aro \clb(nH)$ by $\pi^U(x)= Un\pi(x)U^*$ and rewrite the above identity as $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^U_k(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$ where $\pi^U_k(x)=U\pi_k(x)U^*$. Note that by our construction we can ensure $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ for all $1 \le k \le n$ as the operator intertwining between two imprimitivity systems are acting on the orthogonal subspace of the projection generated by vectors $\{\Omega_k:1 \le k \le n\}$. \vsp We claim $\cle=	ilde{\clf}$. Suppose not i.e. $	ilde{\clf} < \cle$. In such a case we have $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k]$$ Alternatively $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$ \vsp Thus in principle we can repeat our construction now with $\pi^U$ and so we get a strict partial ordered set of quasi-equivalent representation of $\clb$. In the following we now aim to employ formal set theory to bring a contradiction on our starting assumption that $	ilde{\clf} < \cle$. \vsp To that end we need to deal with more then one representation of $\clb$. For the rest of the proof we reset notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ used for the pure representation of $\clb$ in $H_0 =[\pi_0(\clb)\Omega_0]$ where $\Omega_0$ is the cyclic vector, the reset notation for $\Omega$. Let $\clp$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:\clb aro \clb(H_0)$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. $\omega(\pi(	heta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists minimal cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus for such an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega_{\pi})$ we can associate two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$ $\pi_0$ being a pure representation, any element $\pi \in \clp$ is a type-I factor representation of $\clb$. The interesting point here that $\dsp{\oplus_{\pi \in \clp }}\pi$ is also an element in $\clp$ with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ if there exists an isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} aro n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that \vsp \NI (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have $U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some $1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$; \NI (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where $\cle'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(\clb)'$; \NI (C3) $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^1_{\alpha}] < \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$. \vsp In the inequality we explicitly used that both Hilbert spaces are subspaces of $nH_0$ for some possibly larger cardinal number $n$. That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H,\Omega) \prec (\pi,H,\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$. Thus $\pi^U \in \clp$ and by our starting assumption that $	ilde{\clf} 
eq \cle$ we also check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in \clp$ there exists an element $\pi' \in \clp$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus $\clp_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain containing $\pi_0$. \vsp However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset $\clp_0$ of $\clp$ containing $\pi_0$. We claim that $\pi_{max} = \oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in $\clp_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in \clp$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in \clp_0$ there exists an element $(H_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in \clp_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_{\pi_1} aro n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in \clp_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph$. Thus by maximal property of $\clp_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $	ilde{\clf} < \cle$. This completes the proof that $	ilde{\clf}=\cle$ when $\cle 
eq I$. By symmetry of the argument we also get $\clf=	ilde{\cle}$ when $	ilde{\cle} < 1$. \vsp \NI { f Case 2:} $\cle=I \;(	ilde{\cle}=I)$. We need to show $	ilde{\clf}=I\;(\clf=I)$ respectively. Suppose not and assume that both $	ilde{\clf}$ is a proper non-zero projection. \vsp We set projection $G$ on the closed linear span of elements in the subspaces $[	heta^{-n}(\clf)\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]$ for all $n \ge 0$. We recall that $	heta(X)=VXV^*$ where $V=\sum_k S_k	ilde{S}_k^*$ and $	heta^{-1}(X)=	ilde{\Lambda}(X)$ for $X \in \pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. Thus we have $$V^*	heta^{-n}(\clf)\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega$$ $$=	heta^{-n-1}(\clf)V^*\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''V\Omega$$ $$=	heta^{-n-1}(\clf) 	ilde{\Lambda}(\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega.$$ Thus $(1-G)V^*G=0$ i.e. $	heta(G) \ge G$. It is also clear that $	ilde{\clf} \le G$ as the defining sequence of subspaces of $G$ goes to precisely $	ilde{\clf}$ as $n aro \infty$ ( recall that $	heta^{-n}(\clf)=	ilde{\Lambda}_n(\clf) \uparrow I$ strongly as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). Once more we have $	heta^n(G) \ge 	heta^n(	ilde{\clf}) = \Lambda^n(	ilde{\clf}) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$. \vsp If $G$ is a proper projection we can follow the steps as in the case 1 to find a unitary operator $U:nH aro nH$ with $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ and $U ar{V}U^*= ar{V}$ so that $U ar{G}U^*= ar{	ilde{\clf}}$. We consider the subset $\clp_G$ of elements in $\clp$ for which $\cle_{\pi}=1$ and $\{	heta^{-n}(\clf_{\pi}):n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with $	ilde{\clf}_{\pi}$ and modify the strict partial ordering by modifying (C3) as \vsp \NI (C3') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] < \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$ \NI So we also get $\pi^U \in \clp_G$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$ and going along the same line we conclude that $G=	ilde{\clf}$. Thus we conclude that $G$ is either equal to $1$ or $G=	ilde{\clf}$. \vsp \NI { f Sub-case 1 of case 2:} If $G=I$ then $\clf G = \clf$ and so $[\clf\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]=\clf$ as $	heta^{-n}(\clf) \ge \clf$. Thus $	ilde{\clf} \ge \clf$. So $	ilde{\clf} \ge 	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf)$ for all $n \ge 1$ and taking limit we get $	ilde{\clf} \ge I$ i.e. $	ilde{\clf}=I$. This contradicts our starting assumption that $	ilde{\clf}$ is a proper projection. \vsp \NI { f Sub-case 2 of case 2:} Now we consider the case $G=	ilde{\clf} < I$. In such a case we have $(1- 	ilde{\clf})	heta^{-n}(\clf)	ilde{\clf}=0$ and so $	heta^{-n}(\clf)$ commutes with $	ilde{\clf}$ for all $n \ge 0$. \vsp First we rule out the simplest possibility in the present situation for $\clf 	ilde{\clf} = |\Omega><\Omega|$. If so then $\omega$ is a Bernoulli state and a proof follows once we compute the following using the property $\Lambda(	ilde{\clf}) \ge 	ilde{\clf}$ i.e. $	ilde{\clf}\pi(s_i)^*	ilde{\clf} = \pi(s_i)^*	ilde{\clf}$ and commuting property of $\clf$ with $\pi(s_i)^*$ to get some scalars $ ar{\lambda_i}$ such that $$ ar{\lambda}_i= \clf	ilde{\clf}\pi(s_i)^*	ilde{\clf}\clf = \pi(s_i)^*	ilde{\clf}\clf$$ and so $$\omega(s_Is_J^*)=<\Omega,\pi(s_I) \pi(s_J)^*\Omega>$$ $$=<\Omega, \clf 	ilde{\clf} \pi(s_I)\pi(s_J)^*	ilde{\clf}\clf \Omega>$$ $$=\lambda_I\lambda_J^*$$ The inductive limit state $\omega$ on $\clb$, give rises to a pure state once restricted to $\clb_R$ and thus we have $\cle=	ilde{\clf}$ by Haag duality when $\pi(\clb_R)''$ is a type-I factor. This contradicts our starting assumption that $\cle=I$. \vsp Now we set projection $\clf'$ defined by  e \clf'=\clf-\clf	ilde{\clf}+|\Omega><\Omega| \ee and check by commuting property of $	ilde{\clf}$ with $\clf$ that $$ \clf'	heta^{-1}(\clf')\clf' = (I-	ilde{\clf})\clf	heta^{-1}(\clf)(I-	heta^{-1}(	ilde{\clf}))(I-	ilde{\clf})\clf + |\Omega><\Omega|$$ $$= \clf(I-	ilde{\clf}) + |\Omega><\Omega|=\clf'$$ where we have used $	heta^{-1}(\clf) = 	ilde{\Lambda}(\clf) \ge \clf,\; 	heta(\clf) \le \clf$ and $	heta(	ilde{\clf}) = \Lambda(	ilde{\clf}) \ge 	ilde{\clf}$. Thus we get  e 	heta^{-1}(\clf') \ge \clf' \ee \vsp We also rule out the possibility that $\clf 	ilde{\clf} = \clf$. If so then $\clf \le 	ilde{\clf}$ and $	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf) \le 	ilde{\Lambda}^n(	ilde{\clf}) = 	ilde{\clf}$. Taking limit we get $	ilde{\clf}=I$ as $	ilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf) \uparrow I$ as $n aro \infty$. This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis. \vsp So we have in particular $\clf' < \clf \le I$ and $\clf' - |\Omega><\Omega| 
eq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of $\clf=I$ under our hypothesis $	ilde{\clf} < \cle=I$. Suppose so i.e. $\clf=I$, then $	ilde{\cle}=I$ since $	ilde{\cle} \ge \clf$. Then $Q=\cle 	ilde{\cle} = \cle = \cle \clf=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi(\clo_d)'= \pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $	ilde{\clf}=[\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi(\clo_d)'\Omega]=\cle$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $	ilde{\clf} < \cle=I$. \vsp We also have $	heta^{-1}(\clf') \ge \clf'$ and $	heta^{-1}(\clf) \ge \clf$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements $\clf',\clf,	heta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $	ilde{\clf},\cle,	heta$ to get a unitary operator $U:nH aro nH$ so that $U ar{V}= ar{V}U$ and $U ar{\clf}U^*= ar{\clf'}$ for a cardinal number $n$. \vsp Now we consider a further subset $\clp_{G'}$ of $\clp_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ of $\clb$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: $\clf_{\pi} < I, \cle_{\pi}=I$ and $\{	heta^{-n}(	ilde{\clf_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with $\clf_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $(\clh_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec (\clh_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ given by modifying condition (C3') as \vsp \NI (C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] > \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$ \vsp Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in \clp_{G'}$ by covariance relation of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in \clp_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can repeat the process and so $\clp_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$. Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption that $\clf' < \clf$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis that $	ilde{\clf}$ is a proper projection i.e. $\clf < \cle=I$. Thus we arrive at $	ilde{\clf}=\cle$ when $\cle=I$. \vsp By symmetry of argument used here it also follows that $\clf=	ilde{\cle}$ when $	ilde{\cle}=I$. This completes the proof of $	ilde{\clf}=\cle,\;\; \clf =	ilde{\cle}$ for the case when $H$ is the trivial closed subgroup of $S^1$. \vsp Now we will remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial using Proposition 3.4. Let $(H,\pi_0,\Omega)$ be the GNS space of the state $\omega$ on $\clb$. Let $e_0$ and $	ilde{e}_0$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi_0(\clb_R)''$ and $\pi_0(\clb_L)''$ respectively. Similarly we also set projections $\clf_0=[\pi_0(\cla_R)''\Omega]$ and $	ilde{\clf}_0=[\pi_0(\clb_L)''\Omega]$. We also set projections $q_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$ and $p_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$. \vsp $\omega$ being pure, by Theorem 3.4 any $\{ eta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant element of $\clb(	ilde{\clh} \otimes_{\clk} \clh)$ is an element in $\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\cle,	ilde{\cle},\clf, 	ilde{\clf}$ are $\{ eta_z:z \in H \}$ elements. Thus once we identify cyclic space $[\pi_0(\clb)\Omega]$ with $F_0=[\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$, we get obvious relations  e \cle F_0=e_0,	ilde{\cle}F_0=	ilde{e}_0,\clf F_0=f_0, 	ilde{\clf}F_0=	ilde{f}_0 \ee and  e P F_0 = p_0 \;\;\mbox{and} \;\; QF_0=q_0 \ee as $\cle=[\pi(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega]$, $	ilde{\cle} = [\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$, $Q=\cle	ilde{\cle}$ and $P=\cle \clf$. Further $V$ is also $\{  eta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant and $V \pi(x)V^*=\pi(	heta(x))$ for all $x \in \clb$ which we have identified with $	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$. \vsp By applying the first part of the argument with representation $\pi_0$, for pure $\omega$, we have $e_0=	ilde{f}_0$ and $	ilde{e}_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$. \vsp Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as $\cle \clf F_0=\cle	ilde{\cle}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to conclude that $\Lambda(\cle)\clf F_1=\Lambda(\cle)	ilde{\cle} F_1$ and multiplying by $\cle$ from left we get $\cle\clf F_1=\cle	ilde{\cle}F_1$ as $\Lambda(\cle)\cle=\cle$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$. \vsp If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly $	ilde{\clf} = \sum_k 	ilde{\clf}F_k = \sum_k \cle F_k = \cle$ and also $\clf=	ilde{\cle}$. \vsp If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\IZ$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = \Lambda^k(\cle)	ilde{\cle} F_0 - \Lambda^k(\cle)\clf F_0= \Lambda^k(\cle)(	ilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$ Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$. \vsp Now we are left to prove those three statements given in (b). $\omega$ being pure we have $P=Q$ and thus by Proposition 3.5 we have $	ilde{\clm}=\clm'$ and $\pi(\clo_d)'=\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''$. We are left to show $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)'=\pi_{\omega}(\clb_L)''$. For that we recall $F_0$ and check few obvious relation $F_0\pi(\clo_d)'F_0=F_0\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''F_0$ and $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)' \subseteq F_0\pi(\clo_d)'F_0$. Since $F_0\pi(	ilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_0$ is equal to $( eta_z:z \in H)$ invariant elements in $F_0\pi(	ilde{\clo}_d)''F_0$ and elements in $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)'$ are $( eta_z: z \in H)$ invariant we conclude that $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}(\clb_L)''$. Inclusion in other direction is obvious and thus Haag duality property (iii) holds.
nodes.statement_short: One direction: the support-projection hypothesis gives $P=Q$ and an asymptotic condition yielding purity. Converse: build the shift unitary $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde S_k^*$, use Mackey imprimitivity plus Hausdorff maximality to force $\tilde\clf=\cle$ and $\clf=\tilde\cle$, treating $\cle \ne I$ and $\cle=I$ as separate cases; finally remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: hypothesis on the dual support projection gives $\clf=\tilde\cle$ and $\cle=\tilde\clf$
nodes.statement: First we will prove that $\omega$ is pure if $P$ is also the support projection of the state $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''\tilde{\clf}$, where $\tilde{\clf}=[\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''\Omega]$. The support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''\tilde{\clf}$ is $\tilde{\cle}\tilde{\clf}$ and thus we also have $P = \tilde{\cle}\tilde{\clf}$ by our hypothesis. Since $\Lambda^n(P)=\Lambda^n(\cle)\clf \uparrow \clf$ and now $\Lambda^n(P)=\tilde{\cle}\Lambda^n(\tilde{\clf}) \uparrow \tilde{\cle}$ as $n \uparrow \infty$, we also have $\clf = \tilde{\cle}$. Similarly we also have for each $n$, $\cle\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf)=\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{\cle})\tilde{\clf}$ and thus taking limit we also get $\cle=\tilde{\clf}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take limits of $\Lambda^n(P)$ in two ways to identify the four projections.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: consequently $P=Q$ and $[\tilde\clm\Omega]=P$
nodes.statement: So we have $P=\cle \clf=\cle \tilde{\cle}=Q$. $\tilde{\clm}=P\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''P$ is cyclic in $\clk$ i.e. $[\tilde{\clm}\Omega]=[P\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''P\Omega]= P\tilde{\clf}=P\cle=P$ as $\tilde{\clf}=\cle$.
nodes.statement_short: From $\tilde\clf=\cle$ one gets cyclicity of $\Omega$ for $\tilde\clm$ in $\clk$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: asymptotic collapse $\|\Psi\tilde\tau_n-\phi\|\to 0$ on $\tilde\clm_0$
nodes.statement: However $\bigcap_{n \raro \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)) = \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'' \bigcap \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'$ ( for a proof which is a simple application of Cuntz relation, we refer to section 5 of [Mo2]). Further $\psi$ being a factor state in $K_{\omega'}$, by Proposition 3.2 $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is a factor. In particular we have $\bigcap_{n \raro \infty} \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d))\tilde{\clf} = \IC \tilde{\clf}$. Thus by Proposition 1.1 in [Ar2] we conclude that $||\Psi \circ \tilde{\tau}_n -\phi|| \raro 0$ as $n \raro \infty$ for all normal state $\Psi$ on $\tilde{\clm}_0$ where $\tilde{\clm}_0=P \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''P$ as $\tilde{\clf}=\cle$ and support projection of $\psi$ in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$ is $\tilde{\cle}$ and $P=\cle\tilde{\cle}\cle$.
nodes.statement_short: The intersection $\bigcap_n\tilde\Lambda^n(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d))$ is trivial, so Proposition 1.1 of [Ar2] applies.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the gauge-invariant corners $\clm_0,\tilde\clm_0$ and $P_0$
nodes.statement: Note that $\tilde{\clm}_0 \subseteq \clm_0'$ where $\clm_0=P\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)''P$. Further by Proposition 2.5 $\clm_0 = \{x \in \clm:\beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}\;\;\;$ and $\tilde{\clm}_0=\{x \in \tilde{\clm}: \beta_z(x)=x;z \in H \}$. Once we set $P_0=[\clm_0\Omega]$ then we also have $P_0=[\tilde{\clm}_0\Omega]$ as $[\tilde{\clm}\Omega]=P=[\clm\Omega]$ by expending $u_z=\sum_{k \in \hat{H}} z^kP_k$ where $z \raro u_z= PU_zP$ is a unitary representation of group $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Proposition 2.5 identifies $\clm_0,\tilde\clm_0$ as $\beta_z$-fixed points and $P_0=[\clm_0\Omega]=[\tilde\clm_0\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: duality $\phi(\tilde\tau(x)y)=\phi(x\tau(y))$ and conclusion of purity
nodes.statement: For $x \in \tilde{\clm}, y \in \tilde{\clm}'$ we have $$\phi(\tilde{\tau}(x)y)=\sum_k <\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega,x\tilde{v}^*_ky\Omega> = \sum_k <v^*_k\Omega,x y \tilde{v}^*_k\Omega>$$ (as $v_k^*\Omega=\tilde{v}^*_k\Omega$ ) $$=\sum_k <\Omega, x v_kyv_k^* \Omega>=\phi(x \tau(y))$$ The dual group of $(\tilde{\clm},\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given on the commutant by $(\tilde{\clm}',\tau,\phi)$ where $\tau(x)=\sum_k v_k x v_k^*$ for $x \in \tilde{\clm}'$. where commutant is taken in $\clb(\clk)$. Now moving to $\{\beta_z: z \in H \}$ invariant elements in the duality relation above, we verify that adjoint Markov map of $(\tilde{\clm}_0,\tilde{\tau},\phi)$ is given by $(\tilde{\clm}'_0,\tau,\phi)$ where $\tilde{\clm}'_0$, the commutant of $\tilde{\clm}_0$ is taken in $\clb(\clk_0)$ and $\clk_0$ is the Hilbert subspace $P_0$ with $\Omega$ as cyclic and separating vector for $\tilde{\clm}_0$ in $\clk_0$. Thus by Theorem 2.4 in [Mo3], there exists a sequence of elements $y_n \in \tilde{\clm}'_0$ such that for each $m \ge 1$, $y_{m+n}\tau_n(y) \raro \phi(y)1$ as $n \raro \infty$ for all $y \in \tilde{\clm}'_0 \subseteq \clb(\clk_0)$. Thus $\omega$ is pure by Proposition 3.5 (e) once we recall $\clm'=\tilde{\clm}$ as $P=Q$ ( and so $\clm'_0 = \tilde{\clm}_0$ ) by Proposition 3.5 (d). This completes the proof of purity property of $\omega$.
nodes.statement_short: The adjoint Markov map of $(\tilde\clm_0,\tilde\tau,\phi)$ is $(\tilde\clm'_0,\tau,\phi)$, so [Mo3] and Proposition 3.5 give purity.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: start of the hard direction
nodes.statement: In the following we now prove the hardest part of the theorem namely $\tilde{\clf}=\cle$ and $\clf=\tilde{\cle}$ if $\omega$ is pure. Proof uses extensively the general theory of quasi-equivalent representation of a $C^*$ algebra and we refer [BR1, Chapter 2.4.4] as a general reference.
nodes.statement_short: Announce the proof of $\tilde\clf=\cle$, $\clf=\tilde\cle$ for pure $\omega$ using quasi-equivalence theory.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the shift unitary $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde S^*_k$ and the increasing families $\cle_n,\tilde\clf_n$
nodes.statement: We set unitary operator $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde{S}^*_k$. That $V$ is a unitary operator follows by Cuntz's relations and commuting property of $(S_i)$ and $(\tilde{S}_i)$. Further a simple computation shows that $V\pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in \clb = \clb_L \otimes \clb_R$, identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ and $\theta$ is the right shift. We also have \be \theta(\cle)=V \cle V^*= \sum_{k,k'}S_k\tilde{S}^*_k \cle S^*_{k'}\tilde{S}_{k'}=\Lambda(\cle) \ge \cle \ee Similarly we also have \be \theta(\tilde{\clf}) \ge \tilde{\clf} \ee So in particular we have $V(I-\cle)V^* \le I-\cle$, i.e. $(I-\cle)V^*\cle=0$. Also for any $X \in \pi(\clo_d)'$ we have $V^*\tilde{\clf}X\Omega = \tilde{\clf} \sum_k \tilde{S}_k X \tilde{S}_k^*\Omega$ as $S_k^*\Omega =\tilde{S}_k^*\Omega$. Thus $(I-\tilde{\clf})V^*\tilde{\clf}=0$ i.e. $V\tilde{\clf}V^*=\Lambda(\tilde{\clf}) \ge \tilde{\clf}$. Similarly we also have \be \theta^{-1}(\tilde{\cle})=V^*\tilde{\cle}V \ge \tilde{\cle}\;\mbox{and}\; V^* \clf V \ge \clf \ee We also set two family of increasing projections for all natural numbers $n \in \IZ$ as follows \be \cle_n=V^n \cle (V^n)^*,\;\;\tilde{\clf}_n=V^n\tilde{\clf}(V^n)^* \ee
nodes.statement_short: Show $V\pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$, $\theta(\cle)=\Lambda(\cle)\ge\cle$ and define $\cle_n=V^n\cle(V^n)^*$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: weak mixing: $V^n \to |\Omega><\Omega|$, and reduction to trivial $H$
nodes.statement: Since $\beta_z(V)=V$ for all $z \in H$, $V \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$ by Proposition 3.4 as $\omega$ is pure. $\omega$ being also a factor state, we have $<f,V^ng> \raro <f,\Omega><\Omega,g>$ as $n \raro + \mbox{or} - \infty$ for any $f,g \in \pi(\clb_{loc})\Omega$ by Power's criteria [Pow] given in (1). Since such vectors are dense in the Hilbert space topology and the family $\{V^n:n \ge 1\}$ is uniformly bounded, we get $V^n \raro |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology as $n \raro + \mbox{or} - \infty$. \vsp For the time being we assume that $H$ is trivial. Otherwise the argument that follows here we can use for the representation $\pi_0$ of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$ i.e. $\pi$ restricted to $[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. \vsp We have following distinct cases:
nodes.statement_short: Powers' criterion gives the weak limit; if $H$ is nontrivial one works with $\pi_0$ instead.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Case 1: $\cle \ne I$ — the limit $\cle_{-\infty}$ is $|\Omega><\Omega|$ or infinite dimensional
nodes.statement: \NI {\bf Case 1.} $\cle \neq I \;( \tilde{\cle} \neq I)$. Let $\cle_n \raro \cle_{-\infty}$ as $n \raro -\infty$ and thus $V\cle_{-\infty}V^*=\cle_{-\infty}$. We claim that either $\cle_{-\infty} = |\Omega><\Omega|$ or $\cle_{-\infty}$ is a proper infinite dimensional projection i.e. if $\cle_{- \infty}$ is a finite projection then $\cle_{- \infty}=|\Omega><\Omega|$. Suppose not then the finite subspace is shift invariant. In particular there exists a unit vector $f$ orthogonal to $\Omega$ such that $Vf=zf$ for some $z \in S^1$ and this contradicts weak mixing property i.e. $V^n \raro |\Omega><\Omega|$ in weak operator topology proved above as point spectrum of $V$ has only $1$ with spectral multiplicity $1$.
nodes.statement_short: A finite shift-invariant subspace would give an eigenvector of $V$ orthogonal to $\Omega$, contradicting weak mixing.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: imprimitivity systems of Mackey index $\aleph_0$
nodes.statement: If $\cle_{-\infty}$ is infinite dimensional we can get a unitary operator $U_0$ from $F_0=\tilde{\clh} \otimes_{\clk} \clh$ onto $\cle_{- \infty}$ and via the unitary map we can get a sequence of increasing projections $U_0\cle_nU^*_0$ in $\cle_{- \infty}$ and note that $U_0\cle_nU_0^*=V^nU_0 \cle U_0^*(V^n)^*$. Note that if $\cle_{- \infty}$ is infinite dimension the process will not stop in finite step. Thus we have $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{\cle}} F(k)$ where the index set is either singleton or infinity and each $F(k)$ will give a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$, where $F(1) =F_0-\cle_{-\infty}$. Further $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ being a simple $C^*$-algebra, each such imprimitivity system is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ [Mo3,section 4]: We fix a nonzero $f \in \cle-\theta^{-1}(\cle) \neq 0$ otherwise $\cle=I$ as $\theta^n(\cle) \uparrow I$ as $n \raro \infty$. $\pi_f:x \raro \theta^{-1}(x)f$ gives a representation of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d=\clb_L$ and we check that $[\pi_f(\theta^{-1}(\clb_L)''f] \le \cle-\theta^{-1}(\cle)$ as $f \perp [\theta^{-1}(\pi(\clb_R)')\Omega] \ge [\theta^{-1}(\pi(\clb_L))\Omega]$. Thus simplicity ensures that $\cle - \theta^{-1}(\cle)$ is a projection of dimension $\aleph_0$. Further $n_\cle$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$ since $F_0$ is separable.
nodes.statement_short: Simplicity of $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ makes $\cle-\theta^{-1}(\cle)$ infinite dimensional, so $n_\cle \in \{1,\aleph_0\}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: same decomposition for $\tilde\clf$
nodes.statement: Since $\tilde{\clf}$ is also a proper projection, same argument is valid for $\tilde{\clf}$ with $\tilde{\clf}_{-\infty}= \mbox{lim}_{n \raro -\infty} \theta^n(\tilde{\clf})$ i.e. we can write $F_0 \ominus \Omega = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n_{\tilde{\clf}}} \tilde{H}(k)$, where each $\tilde{H}(k)$ give rises to a system of imprimitivity with respect to $V$ where each system of imprimitivity is of Mackey index $\aleph_0$ where $\tilde{F}(1) = F_0-\tilde{\clf}_{-\infty}$ and $n_{\tilde{\clf}}$ is either $1$ or $\aleph_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeat the imprimitivity analysis with $\tilde\clf_{-\infty}$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: amplification notation $n\pi$ on $nH$
nodes.statement: In the following we use temporary notation $H$ for Hilbert subspace $F_0$. For a cardinal number $n$, we amplify a representation $\pi:\clb \raro \clb(H)$ of the $C^*$ algebra $\clb$ to $n$ fold direct sum $n\pi=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } \pi_k $ acting on $nH=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n } H_k$ defining by $$n\pi(x) (\oplus \zeta_k) = \oplus (\pi(x)\zeta_k)$$ where $\pi_k = \pi$ is the representation of $\clb=\mbox{UHF}_d \otimes \tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d$ on $H_k=H$ where $H =[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)\Omega]$. We also extend $\bar{\tilde{F}} = \oplus \tilde{F}_{\alpha}$, $\bar{E} = \oplus E_{\alpha}$ and $\bar{V}=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n} V_k$ respectively. We also set notation $\Omega_k=\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}\delta^k_j\Omega$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the $n$-fold amplification and the amplified projections $\bar\cle,\bar{\tilde\clf},\bar V$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Mackey's theorem gives $U$ with $\bar\cle=U\bar{\tilde\clf}U^*$
nodes.statement: Thus by Mackey's theorem, there exists a cardinal number $n \in \aleph_0$ and a unitary operator $U: nH \raro nH$ so that $\bar{V}=U\bar{V}U^*$ and $\bar{\cle}=U\bar{\tilde{\clf}}U^*$. We set a representation $\pi^U:\clb \raro \clb(nH)$ by $\pi^U(x)= Un\pi(x)U^*$ and rewrite the above identity as $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] = \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^U_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$ where $\pi^U_k(x)=U\pi_k(x)U^*$. Note that by our construction we can ensure $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ for all $1 \le k \le n$ as the operator intertwining between two imprimitivity systems are acting on the orthogonal subspace of the projection generated by vectors $\{\Omega_k:1 \le k \le n\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Intertwining the two imprimitivity systems gives a unitary fixing each $\Omega_k$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: claim $\cle=\tilde\clf$; assume $\tilde\clf < \cle$
nodes.statement: We claim $\cle=\tilde{\clf}$. Suppose not i.e. $\tilde{\clf} < \cle$. In such a case we have $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega_k]$$ Alternatively $$\oplus_{1 \le k \le n}[\pi_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k] < \oplus_{1 \le k \le n} [\pi^u_k(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega_k]$$
nodes.statement_short: The strict inequality transfers to the amplified cyclic subspaces.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: iterating the construction gives a strict partial order
nodes.statement: Thus in principle we can repeat our construction now with $\pi^U$ and so we get a strict partial ordered set of quasi-equivalent representation of $\clb$. In the following we now aim to employ formal set theory to bring a contradiction on our starting assumption that $\tilde{\clf} < \cle$.
nodes.statement_short: Repeating with $\pi^U$ produces an infinite strictly increasing chain of quasi-equivalent representations.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the class $\clp$ for $\clb$ and its cardinal invariants
nodes.statement: To that end we need to deal with more then one representation of $\clb$. For the rest of the proof we reset notation $\pi_0$ for $\pi$ used for the pure representation of $\clb$ in $H_0 =[\pi_0(\clb)\Omega_0]$ where $\Omega_0$ is the cyclic vector, the reset notation for $\Omega$. Let $\clp$ be the collection of representation $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega)$ quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0:\clb \raro \clb(H_0)$ with a shift invariant vector state $\omega(x)=<\Omega,\pi(x)\Omega>$ i.e. $\omega(\pi(\theta(x))=\omega(\pi(x))$. So there exists minimal cardinal numbers $n_{\pi},n_0(\pi)$ so that $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}$ is unitary equivalent to $n_0(\pi)\pi_0$. Thus for such an element $(\pi,H_{\pi},\Omega_{\pi})$ we can associate two cardinal numbers $n_{\pi}$ and $n_0(\pi)$ and without loss of generality we assume that $H_{\pi} \subseteq n_0(\pi)H_0$ and $n_{\pi}H_{\pi}=n_0(\pi)H_0.$ $\pi_0$ being a pure representation, any element $\pi \in \clp$ is a type-I factor representation of $\clb$. The interesting point here that $\dsp{\oplus_{\pi \in \clp }}\pi$ is also an element in $\clp$ with associated cardinal numbers $\sum_{\pi} n_{\pi}$ and $\sum_{\pi} n_0(\pi)$. We say $(\pi_1,H_{\pi_1},\Omega^1) \prec (\pi_2,H_{\pi_2},\Omega^2)$ if there exists an isometry $U:n_{\pi_1} H_{\pi_1} \raro n_{\pi_2} H_{\pi_2}$ so that
nodes.statement_short: Collect all representations quasi-equivalent to $\pi_0$ with a shift-invariant vector state.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: conditions (C1)-(C3) defining $\prec$
nodes.statement: \NI (C1) For each $1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} $ we have $U \Omega^1_{\alpha} = \Omega^2_{\alpha'}$ for some $1 \le \alpha' \le n_{\pi_2}$; \NI (C2) $n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(x)E'_2 = U n_{\pi_1}\pi_1(x) U^* $ where $\cle'_2 \in n_{\pi_2}\pi_2(\clb)'$; \NI (C3) $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^1_{\alpha}] < \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$.
nodes.statement_short: The order requires an isometry preserving cyclic vectors and strictly enlarging $[\pi(\mbox{UHF}_d)'\Omega]$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: non-reflexivity, transitivity, and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$
nodes.statement: In the inequality we explicitly used that both Hilbert spaces are subspaces of $nH_0$ for some possibly larger cardinal number $n$. That the partial order is non-reflexive follows as $(\pi,H,\Omega) \prec (\pi,H,\Omega)$ contradicts (C3) as $I=E_2'$. Partial order property follows easily. If $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ and $\pi_2 \prec \pi_3$ then $\pi_1 \prec \pi_3$. If $U_{12}$ and $U_{23}$ are isometric operators that satisfies (C1)-(C3) respectively, then $U_{13}=U_{23}U_{12}$ will do the job for $\pi_1$ and $\pi_3$. Thus $\pi^U \in \clp$ and by our starting assumption that $\tilde{\clf} \neq \cle$ we also check that $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus going via the isomorphism we also check that for a given element $\pi \in \clp$ there exists an element $\pi' \in \clp$ so that $\pi \prec \pi'$. Thus $\clp_0$ is a non empty set and has at least one infinite chain containing $\pi_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Composition of the intertwiners gives transitivity, and the assumption $\tilde\clf \ne \cle$ gives an infinite chain.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality contradiction closes Case 1
nodes.statement: However by Hausdorff maximality theorem there exists a non-empty maximal totally ordered subset $\clp_0$ of $\clp$ containing $\pi_0$. We claim that $\pi_{max} = \oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} \pi$ on $H_{\pi_{max}}=\oplus_{\pi \in \clp_0} H_{\pi} $ is an upper bound in $\clp_0$. That $\pi_{max} \in \clp$ is obvious. Further given an element $(H_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_1) \in \clp_0$ there exists an element $(H_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_2) \in \clp_0$ so that $\pi_1 \prec \pi_2$ by our starting remark as $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. By extending isometry $U_{12}$ to an isometry from $H_{\pi_1} \raro n_{\pi_{max}} H_{\pi_{max}}$ trivially we get the required isometry that satisfies (C1),(C2) and (C3) where cardinal numbers $n_{\pi_{max}} = \sum_{\pi \in \clp_0} n_{\pi} \in \aleph$. Thus by maximal property of $\clp_0$ we have $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$. This brings a contradiction as by our construction $(\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega) \prec (\pi_{max},H_{\pi_{max}},\Omega)$ as $\pi_{max} \in \clp_0$ but partial order is strict. This contradicts our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{\clf} < \cle$. This completes the proof that $\tilde{\clf}=\cle$ when $\cle \neq I$. By symmetry of the argument we also get $\clf=\tilde{\cle}$ when $\tilde{\cle} < 1$.
nodes.statement_short: The maximal chain contains its own upper bound $\pi_{max}$, contradicting strictness; hence $\tilde\clf=\cle$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Case 2: $\cle=I$, assume $\tilde\clf$ proper
nodes.statement: \NI {\bf Case 2:} $\cle=I \;(\tilde{\cle}=I)$. We need to show $\tilde{\clf}=I\;(\clf=I)$ respectively. Suppose not and assume that both $\tilde{\clf}$ is a proper non-zero projection.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the remaining case where the support projection is everything.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the auxiliary projection $G$ with $\theta(G) \ge G$ and $\tilde\clf \le G$
nodes.statement: We set projection $G$ on the closed linear span of elements in the subspaces $[\theta^{-n}(\clf)\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]$ for all $n \ge 0$. We recall that $\theta(X)=VXV^*$ where $V=\sum_k S_k\tilde{S}_k^*$ and $\theta^{-1}(X)=\tilde{\Lambda}(X)$ for $X \in \pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''$. Thus we have $$V^*\theta^{-n}(\clf)\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega$$ $$=\theta^{-n-1}(\clf)V^*\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''V\Omega$$ $$=\theta^{-n-1}(\clf) \tilde{\Lambda}(\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega.$$ Thus $(1-G)V^*G=0$ i.e. $\theta(G) \ge G$. It is also clear that $\tilde{\clf} \le G$ as the defining sequence of subspaces of $G$ goes to precisely $\tilde{\clf}$ as $n \raro \infty$ ( recall that $\theta^{-n}(\clf)=\tilde{\Lambda}_n(\clf) \uparrow I$ strongly as $n \uparrow \infty$ ). Once more we have $\theta^n(G) \ge \theta^n(\tilde{\clf}) = \Lambda^n(\tilde{\clf}) \uparrow I$ as $n \uparrow \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: $G$ is spanned by $[\theta^{-n}(\clf)\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]$ and satisfies $(1-G)V^*G=0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: either $G=I$ or $G=\tilde\clf$
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a proper projection we can follow the steps as in the case 1 to find a unitary operator $U:nH \raro nH$ with $U\Omega_k=\Omega_k$ and $U\bar{V}U^*=\bar{V}$ so that $U\bar{G}U^*=\bar{\tilde{\clf}}$. We consider the subset $\clp_G$ of elements in $\clp$ for which $\cle_{\pi}=1$ and $\{\theta^{-n}(\clf_{\pi}):n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with $\tilde{\clf}_{\pi}$ and modify the strict partial ordering by modifying (C3) as \vsp \NI (C3') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] < \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$ \NI So we also get $\pi^U \in \clp_G$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$ and going along the same line we conclude that $G=\tilde{\clf}$. Thus we conclude that $G$ is either equal to $1$ or $G=\tilde{\clf}$.
nodes.statement_short: If $G$ is proper, the Case-1 machinery applied to $\clp_G$ with (C3') forces $G=\tilde\clf$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Sub-case 1 of case 2: $G=I$ gives $\tilde\clf=I$
nodes.statement: \NI {\bf Sub-case 1 of case 2:} If $G=I$ then $\clf G = \clf$ and so $[\clf\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''\Omega]=\clf$ as $\theta^{-n}(\clf) \ge \clf$. Thus $\tilde{\clf} \ge \clf$. So $\tilde{\clf} \ge \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf)$ for all $n \ge 1$ and taking limit we get $\tilde{\clf} \ge I$ i.e. $\tilde{\clf}=I$. This contradicts our starting assumption that $\tilde{\clf}$ is a proper projection.
nodes.statement_short: Then $\clf \le \tilde\clf$ and $\tilde\Lambda^n(\clf)\uparrow I$ force $\tilde\clf=I$, a contradiction.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Sub-case 2 of case 2: $G=\tilde\clf < I$ makes $\theta^{-n}(\clf)$ commute with $\tilde\clf$
nodes.statement: \NI {\bf Sub-case 2 of case 2:} Now we consider the case $G=\tilde{\clf} < I$. In such a case we have $(1- \tilde{\clf})\theta^{-n}(\clf)\tilde{\clf}=0$ and so $\theta^{-n}(\clf)$ commutes with $\tilde{\clf}$ for all $n \ge 0$.
nodes.statement_short: $(1-\tilde\clf)\theta^{-n}(\clf)\tilde\clf=0$ gives the commutation.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: ruling out $\clf\tilde\clf=|\Omega><\Omega|$ (Bernoulli case)
nodes.statement: First we rule out the simplest possibility in the present situation for $\clf \tilde{\clf} = |\Omega><\Omega|$. If so then $\omega$ is a Bernoulli state and a proof follows once we compute the following using the property $\Lambda(\tilde{\clf}) \ge \tilde{\clf}$ i.e. $\tilde{\clf}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{\clf} = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{\clf}$ and commuting property of $\clf$ with $\pi(s_i)^*$ to get some scalars $\bar{\lambda_i}$ such that $$\bar{\lambda}_i= \clf\tilde{\clf}\pi(s_i)^*\tilde{\clf}\clf = \pi(s_i)^*\tilde{\clf}\clf$$ and so $$\omega(s_Is_J^*)=<\Omega,\pi(s_I) \pi(s_J)^*\Omega>$$ $$=<\Omega, \clf \tilde{\clf} \pi(s_I)\pi(s_J)^*\tilde{\clf}\clf \Omega>$$ $$=\lambda_I\lambda_J^*$$ The inductive limit state $\omega$ on $\clb$, give rises to a pure state once restricted to $\clb_R$ and thus we have $\cle=\tilde{\clf}$ by Haag duality when $\pi(\clb_R)''$ is a type-I factor. This contradicts our starting assumption that $\cle=I$.
nodes.statement_short: Then $\omega(s_Is_J^*)=\lambda_I\lambda^*_J$ is a product state, whose right restriction is type-I, contradicting $\cle=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the projection $\clf'=\clf-\clf\tilde\clf+|\Omega><\Omega|$ satisfies $\theta^{-1}(\clf')\ge\clf'$
nodes.statement: Now we set projection $\clf'$ defined by \be \clf'=\clf-\clf\tilde{\clf}+|\Omega><\Omega| \ee and check by commuting property of $\tilde{\clf}$ with $\clf$ that $$ \clf'\theta^{-1}(\clf')\clf' = (I-\tilde{\clf})\clf\theta^{-1}(\clf)(I-\theta^{-1}(\tilde{\clf}))(I-\tilde{\clf})\clf + |\Omega><\Omega|$$ $$= \clf(I-\tilde{\clf}) + |\Omega><\Omega|=\clf'$$ where we have used $\theta^{-1}(\clf) = \tilde{\Lambda}(\clf) \ge \clf,\; \theta(\clf) \le \clf$ and $\theta(\tilde{\clf}) = \Lambda(\tilde{\clf}) \ge \tilde{\clf}$. Thus we get \be \theta^{-1}(\clf') \ge \clf' \ee
nodes.statement_short: A direct computation using commutation of $\clf$ and $\tilde\clf$ gives $\clf'\theta^{-1}(\clf')\clf'=\clf'$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: ruling out $\clf\tilde\clf=\clf$
nodes.statement: We also rule out the possibility that $\clf \tilde{\clf} = \clf$. If so then $\clf \le \tilde{\clf}$ and $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf) \le \tilde{\Lambda}^n(\tilde{\clf}) = \tilde{\clf}$. Taking limit we get $\tilde{\clf}=I$ as $\tilde{\Lambda}^n(\clf) \uparrow I$ as $n \raro \infty$. This brings a contradiction to our hypothesis.
nodes.statement_short: That would give $\clf \le \tilde\clf$ and hence $\tilde\clf=I$, contrary to hypothesis.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: ruling out $\clf=I$
nodes.statement: So we have in particular $\clf' < \clf \le I$ and $\clf' - |\Omega><\Omega| \neq 0$. Now we will rule out the possibility of $\clf=I$ under our hypothesis $\tilde{\clf} < \cle=I$. Suppose so i.e. $\clf=I$, then $\tilde{\cle}=I$ since $\tilde{\cle} \ge \clf$. Then $Q=\cle \tilde{\cle} = \cle = \cle \clf=P$. Thus by Proposition 3.5 (e) we get $\pi(\clo_d)'= \pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''$ and so we have in particular $\tilde{\clf}=[\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''\Omega]=[\pi(\clo_d)'\Omega]=\cle$. This contradicts our starting assumption once more that $\tilde{\clf} < \cle=I$.
nodes.statement_short: $\clf=I$ gives $P=Q$, hence $\tilde\clf=\cle$ by Proposition 3.5 (e), contradicting $\tilde\clf<\cle=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Case-1 machinery applied to $(\clf',\clf,\theta^{-1})$
nodes.statement: We also have $\theta^{-1}(\clf') \ge \clf'$ and $\theta^{-1}(\clf) \ge \clf$. Thus we can follow the steps of Case-1 with elements $\clf',\clf,\theta^{-1}$ replacing the role of $\tilde{\clf},\cle,\theta$ to get a unitary operator $U:nH \raro nH$ so that $U\bar{V}=\bar{V}U$ and $U\bar{\clf}U^*=\bar{\clf'}$ for a cardinal number $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Get a unitary $U$ with $U\bar\clf U^*=\bar{\clf'}$ commuting with $\bar V$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: the class $\clp_{G'}$ with (C3'') and the final contradiction
nodes.statement: Now we consider a further subset $\clp_{G'}$ of $\clp_G$ consist of quasi-equivalent representations $\pi$ to $\pi_0$ of $\clb$ where $\pi$ admits the additional property: $\clf_{\pi} < I, \cle_{\pi}=I$ and $\{\theta^{-n}(\tilde{\clf_{\pi}}): n \ge 0 \}$ commutes with $\clf_{\pi}$ with the strict partial ordering $(\clh_{\pi_1},\pi_1,\Omega_{\pi_1}) \prec (\clh_{\pi_2},\pi_2,\Omega_{\pi_2})$ given by modifying condition (C3') as \vsp \NI (C3'') $\oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_1} }[\pi^{\alpha}_1(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^1_{\alpha}] > \oplus_{1 \le \alpha \le n_{\pi_2}}[\pi^{\alpha}_2(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega^2_{\alpha}]E'_2$ \vsp Since $\pi^U$ also satisfies the conditions that of $\pi_0 \in \clp_{G'}$ by covariance relation of $U$ with respect to shifts once more we get $\pi^U \in \clp_{G'}$ and $\pi_0 \prec \pi^U$. Thus we can repeat the process and so $\clp_{G'}$ has at least one infinite chain of totally ordered containing $\pi_0$. Once more by Hausdorff maximality principle we bring a contradiction to our starting assumption that $\clf' < \clf$. In other words this brings a contradiction to our starting hypothesis that $\tilde{\clf}$ is a proper projection i.e. $\clf < \cle=I$. Thus we arrive at $\tilde{\clf}=\cle$ when $\cle=I$.
nodes.statement_short: A second Hausdorff-maximality argument contradicts $\clf'<\clf$, so $\tilde\clf=\cle$ also when $\cle=I$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: symmetric conclusion $\clf=\tilde\cle$ for trivial $H$
nodes.statement: By symmetry of argument used here it also follows that $\clf=\tilde{\cle}$ when $\tilde{\cle}=I$. This completes the proof of $\tilde{\clf}=\cle,\;\; \clf =\tilde{\cle}$ for the case when $H$ is the trivial closed subgroup of $S^1$.
nodes.statement_short: By symmetry of the argument the dual identity also holds.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: removing the assumption that $H$ is trivial: notation on the GNS space of $\omega$
nodes.statement: Now we will remove the assumption that $H$ is trivial using Proposition 3.4. Let $(H,\pi_0,\Omega)$ be the GNS space of the state $\omega$ on $\clb$. Let $e_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0$ be the support projections of $\omega$ in $\pi_0(\clb_R)''$ and $\pi_0(\clb_L)''$ respectively. Similarly we also set projections $\clf_0=[\pi_0(\cla_R)''\Omega]$ and $\tilde{\clf}_0=[\pi_0(\clb_L)''\Omega]$. We also set projections $q_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$ and $p_0=[\pi_0(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega] [\pi_0(\mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $e_0,\tilde e_0,\clf_0,\tilde\clf_0,q_0,p_0$ in the GNS space of $(\clb,\omega)$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: identification of the projections with their compressions to $F_0$
nodes.statement: $\omega$ being pure, by Theorem 3.4 any $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant element of $\clb(\tilde{\clh} \otimes_{\clk} \clh)$ is an element in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$. $\cle,\tilde{\cle},\clf, \tilde{\clf}$ are $\{\beta_z:z \in H \}$ elements. Thus once we identify cyclic space $[\pi_0(\clb)\Omega]$ with $F_0=[\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''\Omega]$, we get obvious relations \be \cle F_0=e_0,\tilde{\cle}F_0=\tilde{e}_0,\clf F_0=f_0, \tilde{\clf}F_0=\tilde{f}_0 \ee and \be P F_0 = p_0 \;\;\mbox{and} \;\; QF_0=q_0 \ee as $\cle=[\pi(\mbox{UHF})'\Omega]$, $\tilde{\cle} = [\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)'\Omega]$, $Q=\cle\tilde{\cle}$ and $P=\cle \clf$. Further $V$ is also $\{ \beta_z:z \in H \}$ invariant and $V \pi(x)V^*=\pi(\theta(x))$ for all $x \in \clb$ which we have identified with $\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Purity and Proposition 3.4 put all four projections in $\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d \otimes \mbox{UHF}_d)''$, giving $\cle F_0=e_0$ etc.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: applying the trivial-$H$ result to $\pi_0$
nodes.statement: By applying the first part of the argument with representation $\pi_0$, for pure $\omega$, we have $e_0=\tilde{f}_0$ and $\tilde{e}_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Get $e_0=\tilde f_0$, $\tilde e_0=f_0$ and $p_0=q_0$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: propagating $p_0=q_0$ by $\Lambda$ to all $F_m$, $m \ge 0$
nodes.statement: Now we write the equality $p_0=q_0$ as $\cle \clf F_0=\cle\tilde{\cle}F_0$ and apply $\Lambda$ on both side to conclude that $\Lambda(\cle)\clf F_1=\Lambda(\cle)\tilde{\cle} F_1$ and multiplying by $\cle$ from left we get $\cle\clf F_1=\cle\tilde{\cle}F_1$ as $\Lambda(\cle)\cle=\cle$ and thus we get $PF_1=QF_1$. By repeated application of $\Lambda$, we get $PF_m=QF_m$.
nodes.statement_short: Applying $\Lambda$ and multiplying by $\cle$ gives $PF_m=QF_m$.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: finite $H$: summing over $k$ gives $P=Q$
nodes.statement: If $H=\{z:z^n=1 \}$ then we get $P=\sum_k PF_k=\sum_k QF_k=Q$. This completes the proof for $P=Q$. Similarly $\tilde{\clf} = \sum_k \tilde{\clf}F_k = \sum_k \cle F_k = \cle$ and also $\clf=\tilde{\cle}$.
nodes.statement_short: For $H=\{z: z^n=1\}$ sum the identities over the finite dual group.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: $H=S^1$: extending $PF_m=QF_m$ to $m<0$
nodes.statement: If $H=S^1$ then $\hat{H}=\IZ$ and for $m \ge 0$, we have $PF_m=QF_m$. For $m < 0$ we take $k=-m$ and check that $\Lambda^k(QF_m-PF_m)=\Lambda^k(Q)F_{m+k}-\Lambda^k(P)F_{m+k} = \Lambda^k(\cle)\tilde{\cle} F_0 - \Lambda^k(\cle)\clf F_0= \Lambda^k(\cle)(\tilde{e}_0 - f_0)=0$ Since $\Lambda$ is an injective map, we get $QF_m=PF_m$ for all $m < 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply $\Lambda^k$ and use injectivity of $\Lambda$ to reach the negative indices.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: proof of (b): $\clm'=\tilde\clm$, $\pi(\clo_d)'=\pi(\tilde\clo_d)''$ and Haag duality
nodes.statement: Now we are left to prove those three statements given in (b). $\omega$ being pure we have $P=Q$ and thus by Proposition 3.5 we have $\tilde{\clm}=\clm'$ and $\pi(\clo_d)'=\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''$. We are left to show $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)'=\pi_{\omega}(\clb_L)''$. For that we recall $F_0$ and check few obvious relation $F_0\pi(\clo_d)'F_0=F_0\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''F_0$ and $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)' \subseteq F_0\pi(\clo_d)'F_0$. Since $F_0\pi(\tilde{\mbox{UHF}}_d)''F_0$ is equal to $(\beta_z:z \in H)$ invariant elements in $F_0\pi(\tilde{\clo}_d)''F_0$ and elements in $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)'$ are $(\beta_z: z \in H)$ invariant we conclude that $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)' \subseteq \pi_{\omega}(\clb_L)''$. Inclusion in other direction is obvious and thus Haag duality property (iii) holds.
nodes.statement_short: Compressing to $F_0$ and using gauge invariance gives $\pi_\omega(\clb_R)'\subseteq\pi_\omega(\clb_L)''$, the reverse being obvious.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement: (of Theorem 1.1:) (a) implies that $q_0=p_0$. (d) also says that $p_0=q_0$. Thus in either case, following last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6 we get $P=Q$. The statement (e) also implies $P=Q$. That shows now that (a),(d) as well as (e) implies (f) by the if part of Theorem 2.6 (a). That (b) implies (a) is trivial as $\Omega$ is separating for $\clm_1,\tilde{\clm}_1$ by faithful property. That (c) implies (f) is trivial as $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)''$ is a factor. Thus we have showed so far any of the statement (a),(b),(c),(d),(e) implies (f). For the converse we appeal to the only if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.statement_short: Each of (a),(d),(e) gives $P=Q$; (b) and (c) reduce to (a) and the factor property; the converse is the only-if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: (a), (d), (e) each give $P=Q$
nodes.statement: (of Theorem 1.1:) (a) implies that $q_0=p_0$. (d) also says that $p_0=q_0$. Thus in either case, following last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6 we get $P=Q$. The statement (e) also implies $P=Q$.
nodes.statement_short: Each of the three conditions yields $p_0=q_0$ and hence $P=Q$ by the last part of the proof of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: all of (a)-(e) imply (f)
nodes.statement: That shows now that (a),(d) as well as (e) implies (f) by the if part of Theorem 2.6 (a). That (b) implies (a) is trivial as $\Omega$ is separating for $\clm_1,\tilde{\clm}_1$ by faithful property. That (c) implies (f) is trivial as $\pi_{\omega}(\clb_R)''$ is a factor. Thus we have showed so far any of the statement (a),(b),(c),(d),(e) implies (f).
nodes.statement_short: (b) implies (a) since $\Omega$ is separating, and (c) implies (f) since $\pi_\omega(\clb_R)''$ is a factor.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states

nodes.name: converse from Theorem 3.6
nodes.statement: For the converse we appeal to the only if part of Theorem 3.6.
nodes.statement_short: The only-if part of Theorem 3.6 closes the equivalence.
nodes.section: 3 Dual Popescu system and pure translation invariant states
